memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They must no longer offer any of their sacrifices to the goat idols to whom they prostitute themselves. This is to be a lasting ordinance for them and for the generations to come." - Lev 17:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Goat idols. This is a glimpse of what Israel had absorbed in Egypt and had not left behind.

They had walked out of Egypt physically. Spiritually, some of Egypt had walked out with them. They had seen the plagues, crossed the sea, watched an army drown — and they were still, quietly, sacrificing to the old gods.

The word God uses is strong: prostitute themselves. He does not describe idolatry as a lapse in judgement. He describes it as unfaithfulness in a marriage. That is how personally God takes it, because that is how personally He loves.

We should be honest that we do the same. We can be genuinely converted and still carry old gods with us. The need for approval that governs our decisions. The money we trust more than we admit. The relationship we cannot let go of, though it pulls us away from Christ. Nobody builds a shrine any more. We simply keep something at the centre that belongs to God alone.

John ends his letter with an abrupt sentence that has puzzled readers for centuries: Dear children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). He is writing to Christians.

What did you bring out of Egypt that you have never put down?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you carried out of your old life that still holds influence?
2. What sits at the centre of your life that belongs to God alone?
3. Why does God describe idolatry in the language of unfaithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, show me the old gods I have quietly carried with me. Forgive my unfaithfulness, and let nothing take the place that belongs to You alone. Amen.
